lesson_scope: Dihedral angles between intersecting planes, line of intersection derivation, perpendicular distance between parallel planes, lines with orthogonality constraints in planes, line-plane angles, flight descent paths, and multi-face pyramid geometry synthesis.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Acute angle between two planes from normals.

walkthrough.text:
Extract the normal vectors from the plane equations:
$$\mathbf{n}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{n}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the scalar product and magnitudes:
$$\mathbf{n}_1 \cdot \mathbf{n}_2 = 2(1) + 3(-2) + (-1)(1) = -5$$
$$|\mathbf{n}_1| = \sqrt{2^2 + 3^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{14}, \quad |\mathbf{n}_2| = \sqrt{1^2 + (-2)^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{6}$$

Evaluate the acute dihedral angle $\theta$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{|\mathbf{n}_1 \cdot \mathbf{n}_2|}{|\mathbf{n}_1| |\mathbf{n}_2|} = \frac{5}{\sqrt{14 \times 6}} = \frac{5}{\sqrt{84}}$$
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{\sqrt{84}}\right) \approx 56.9^\circ$$

hints: Distance formula between parallel planes is $\frac{|d_2 - d_1|}{|\mathbf{n}|}$.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the magnitude of the shared normal vector $\mathbf{n} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$|\mathbf{n}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 2^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{9} = 3$$

Apply the parallel plane perpendicular distance formula:
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{|14 - 5|}{3} = \frac{9}{3} = 3$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Parallel plane constant shifting nearer to origin.

hints: Moving 1 unit nearer to the origin reduces constant by $1 \times 3 = 3$.
New constant is $k = 5 - 3 = 2$, giving equation $2x + 2y - z = 2$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the constant shift required for a distance of 1 unit:
$$\Delta d = (\text{distance}) \times |\mathbf{n}| = 1 \times 3 = 3$$

Subtract 3 from the constant to move closer to the origin:
$$k = 5 - 3 = 2 \implies 2x + 2y - z = 2$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Cross product direction vector of line of intersection.

walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the cross product $\mathbf{n}_1 \times \mathbf{n}_2$:
$$\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3(1) - (-1)(-2) \\ (-1)(1) - 2(1) \\ 2(-2) - 3(1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \\ -7 \end{pmatrix}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Angle between line and plane using sine formula.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the scalar product and magnitudes:
$$\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n} = 1(2) + 2(-1) + 2(2) = 4$$
$$|\mathbf{d}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2 + 2^2} = 3, \quad |\mathbf{n}| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-1)^2 + 2^2} = 3$$

Calculate the acute angle $\alpha$ using the sine formula:
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{|\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n}|}{|\mathbf{d}| |\mathbf{n}|} = \frac{4}{3 \times 3} = \frac{4}{9}$$
$$\alpha = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{9}\right) \approx 26.4^\circ$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Solving for a common point on two planes.

hints: Substitute $x = 1$ into both equations: $3y - z = -1$ and $-2y + z = 2$.
Add the two equations to eliminate $z$: $y = 1$.
Substitute $y = 1$ into $-2(1) + z = 2 \implies z = 4$. The point is $(1, 1, 4)$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $x = 1$ into the two plane equations:
$$2(1) + 3y - z = 1 \implies 3y - z = -1 \quad \text{--- (1)}$$
$$1 - 2y + z = 3 \implies -2y + z = 2 \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

Add equations (1) and (2) and solve:
$$(3y - z) + (-2y + z) = -1 + 2 \implies y = 1$$
$$z = 2 + 2(1) = 4$$
The common point is $(1, 1, 4)$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $x = 1$ and forms system in $y, z$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Dihedral angle and line of intersection vector equation.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the scalar product and magnitudes of the normals:
$$\mathbf{n}_1 \cdot \mathbf{n}_2 = 2(1) + 3(-2) + (-1)(1) = -5$$
$$|\mathbf{n}_1| = \sqrt{14}, \quad |\mathbf{n}_2| = \sqrt{6}$$

Evaluate the acute angle:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{|-5|}{\sqrt{14 \times 6}} = \frac{5}{\sqrt{84}} \implies \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{\sqrt{84}}\right) \approx 56.9^\circ$$

parts.label: (b)
hints: Find common point by setting $x = 1 \implies y = 1, z = 4 \implies (1, 1, 4)$.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the direction vector of the line of intersection:
$$\mathbf{d} = \mathbf{n}_1 \times \mathbf{n}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \\ -7 \end{pmatrix}$$

Find a particular point by setting $x = 1$:
$$3y - z = -1 \quad \text{and} \quad -2y + z = 2 \implies y = 1, z = 4 \implies (1, 1, 4)$$

State the vector equation of the intersection line:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -3 \\ -7 \end{pmatrix}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Complete line of intersection derivation from two planes.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the cross product of the normal vectors:
$$\mathbf{d} = \mathbf{n}_1 \times \mathbf{n}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1(2) - (-1)(-1) \\ (-1)(1) - 3(2) \\ 3(-1) - 1(1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -7 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$$

Find a particular point on both planes by setting $x = 1$:
$$3(1) + y - z = 2 \implies y - z = -1 \quad \text{--- (1)}$$
$$1 - y + 2z = 1 \implies -y + 2z = 0 \implies y = 2z \quad \text{--- (2)}$$
$$2z - z = -1 \implies z = -1, \ y = -2 \implies (1, -2, -1)$$

State the vector line equation:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -7 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: Distance from origin and parallel planes at fixed distance.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the modulus of the normal vector:
$$|\mathbf{n}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 2^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{9} = 3$$

Calculate the distance from the origin $O(0, 0, 0)$ to plane $m$:
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{|0 - 5|}{3} = \frac{5}{3}$$

parts.label: (b)
hints: Write parallel planes as $2x + 2y - z = k$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the distance equation for parallel planes $2x + 2y - z = k$:
$$\frac{|k - 5|}{3} = 2 \implies |k - 5| = 6$$

Solve for the two possible constants:
$$k - 5 = 6 \implies k = 11$$
$$k - 5 = -6 \implies k = -1$$
The two equations are $2x + 2y - z = 11$ and $2x + 2y - z = -1$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Core: In-plane line with dual orthogonality and angle with axis.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Line in plane perpendicular to OP.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the cross product between the plane normal and position vector $\vec{OP}$:
$$\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \\ -8 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 2 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4(-2) - (-8)(2) \\ (-8)(5) - 1(-2) \\ 1(2) - 4(5) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 8 \\ -38 \\ -18 \end{pmatrix} = 2\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -19 \\ -9 \end{pmatrix}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up cross product or simultaneous scalar products.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Line equation and angle with coordinate axis.

walkthrough.text:
State the vector line equation using base point $P(5, 2, -2)$:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 2 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -19 \\ -9 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the magnitude of the direction vector:
$$|\mathbf{d}| = \sqrt{4^2 + (-19)^2 + (-9)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 361 + 81} = \sqrt{458}$$

Calculate the acute angle with the $x$-axis:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{|\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{i}|}{|\mathbf{d}|} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{458}} \implies \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{458}}\right) \approx 79.2^\circ$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Capstone: Flight descent path touchdown point and angle of approach.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute the parametric descent path into the runway plane equation:
$$(10 - 3\lambda) + 2(20 - 4\lambda) + 2(4 - \lambda) = 6$$
$$10 - 3\lambda + 40 - 8\lambda + 8 - 2\lambda = 6$$
$$58 - 13\lambda = 6 \implies 13\lambda = 52 \implies \lambda = 4$$

Evaluate the touchdown coordinates $T$:
$$T = (10 - 3(4), 20 - 4(4), 4 - 4) = (-2, 4, 0)$$

Compute the scalar product and magnitudes for line direction $\mathbf{d}$ and plane normal $\mathbf{n}$:
$$|\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n}| = |-3(1) - 4(2) - 1(2)| = 13$$
$$|\mathbf{d}| = \sqrt{(-3)^2 + (-4)^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{26}, \quad |\mathbf{n}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2 + 2^2} = 3$$

Calculate the acute angle of descent $\alpha$:
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{|\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n}|}{|\mathbf{d}| |\mathbf{n}|} = \frac{13}{3\sqrt{26}} = \frac{\sqrt{26}}{6}$$
$$\alpha = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{26}}{6}\right) \approx 58.2^\circ$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Capstone: Multiple dihedral angles in prism slicing geometry.

walkthrough.text: Extract the normal vectors: $\mathbf{n}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}, \mathbf{n}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$.

Calculate the acute angle $\theta$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{|\mathbf{n}_2 \cdot \mathbf{n}_1|}{|\mathbf{n}_2| |\mathbf{n}_1|} = \frac{3(1) + 0 + 0}{5 \times 1} = \frac{3}{5} = 0.6$$
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}(0.6) \approx 53.1^\circ$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Dihedral angle between slicing plane and face.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the scalar product and magnitudes for $\mathbf{n}_3 = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{n}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\mathbf{n}_3 \cdot \mathbf{n}_2 = 2(3) + (-1)(0) + 2(4) = 6 + 8 = 14$$
$$|\mathbf{n}_3| = 3, \quad |\mathbf{n}_2| = 5$$

Calculate the acute dihedral angle $\phi$:
$$\cos\phi = \frac{14}{3 \times 5} = \frac{14}{15} \implies \phi = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{14}{15}\right) \approx 21.0^\circ$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Capstone: Complete 3D pyramid dihedral angle, edge intersection, and edge-base angle synthesis.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the scalar product and magnitudes of the two face normals:
$$\mathbf{n}_1 \cdot \mathbf{n}_2 = 0(3) + 3(0) + (-1)(1) = -1$$
$$|\mathbf{n}_1| = \sqrt{0^2 + 3^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{10}, \quad |\mathbf{n}_2| = \sqrt{3^2 + 0^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{10}$$

Evaluate the acute dihedral angle $\theta$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{|\mathbf{n}_1 \cdot \mathbf{n}_2|}{|\mathbf{n}_1| |\mathbf{n}_2|} = \frac{1}{10} = 0.1 \implies \theta = \cos^{-1}(0.1) \approx 84.3^\circ$$

Compute the direction vector of the line of intersection of the two faces:
$$\mathbf{d} = \mathbf{n}_1 \times \mathbf{n}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 - 0 \\ -3 - 0 \\ 0 - 9 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -3 \\ -9 \end{pmatrix} \sim \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$$

Use the apex point $V(2, 2, 6)$ to write the vector equation of edge $VB$:
$$\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the scalar product and magnitudes for edge direction $\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$ and base normal $\mathbf{n}_{\text{base}} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$|\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n}_{\text{base}}| = |1(0) - 1(0) - 3(1)| = 3$$
$$|\mathbf{d}| = \sqrt{1^2 + (-1)^2 + (-3)^2} = \sqrt{11}, \quad |\mathbf{n}_{\text{base}}| = 1$$

Calculate the acute angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal base:
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{|\mathbf{d} \cdot \mathbf{n}_{\text{base}}|}{|\mathbf{d}| |\mathbf{n}_{\text{base}}|} = \frac{3}{\sqrt{11}}$$
$$\alpha = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{11}}\right) \approx 64.8^\circ$$
